html:
On 2 August 1858 the British Parliament passed the Government of India Act, which ended the rule of the East India Company and put India directly under the Crown. The period that followed, to 1947, is called the Raj.

The cause was the Indian Rebellion of 1857. A trading company had ruled a subcontinent for a century, and Parliament judged that it had failed.

The changes:

  • A cabinet minister in London, the Secretary of State for India, took charge, advised by a council.
  • The governor-general gained the title of viceroy, the queen's deputy.
  • The Company's army passed to the Crown. The number of British soldiers was raised to about one for every two Indians, and the artillery was kept in British hands.

On 1 November 1858 Queen Victoria's proclamation was read out at Allahabad and other cities. It promised no more annexations (see the doctrine of lapse), respect for the treaties with the princes, no interference with religion, and that Indians could hold any office for which they were fit. Nationalists later quoted that last promise back at the government.

The last Mughal emperor was exiled to Rangoon (see the Mughal Empire). Victoria was declared Empress of India in 1877. See British rule.
